Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:10:1.english: From where are these matters [derived] - That his own [property] takes precedence.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:10:2.english: There shall be no needy among you - Guard against poverty.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:11:1.hebrew: כל המקיים בעצמו כך - אף על פי שלא הטילו עליו הכתוב, יש לאדם ליכנס לפנים משורת הדין, ולא לדקדק "שלי קודם" אם לא בהפסד מוכיח. ואם תמיד מדקדק, פורק מעליו עול ג"ח וצדקה, וסוף שיצטרך לבריות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:11:1.english: Anyone who fulfills this with regard to himself - Even though Scripture did not impose it upon him, a person should act beyond the letter of the law, and not be exacting [by saying] "mine comes first," unless there is an evident loss. And if he is always exacting, he casts off from himself the yoke of acts of lovingkindness and charity, and ultimately he will come to need [the help of] other people.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:12:1.hebrew: שלמדו חכמה - סברת טעמי המשנה, ולהבין שלא יהו סותרות זו את זו, וטעמי איסור והיתר והחיוב והפטור, והוא נקרא גמרא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:12:1.english: Who taught him wisdom - The reasoning behind the rationales of the Mishnah, and [how] to understand [the mishnayot] so that they do not contradict one another, and the reasons for prohibition and permission, and liability and exemption; and this is called Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:12:3.hebrew: משנה - כמו שהן שנויות, ואין טעמן מפורש בהן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:12:3.english: Mishna - As they are taught, and their reason is not explained in them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:12:4.hebrew: כל שרוב חכמתו הימנו - אם מקרא, אם משנה, אם גמרא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:12:4.english: Any [teacher] from whom most of his wisdom [comes] - Whether Bible, whether Mishnah, [or] whether Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:12:5.english: Enlightened his eyes - That he informed him of the reason for one mishnah that he could not understand.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:1.hebrew: דאסברן זוהמא ליסטרון - בסדר טהרות (כלים פי"ב משנה ב ופכ"ה משנה ג) היא שנויה, ולא הייתי יודע מה כלי הוא, ולמדני שהוא כף גדולה שמסלקין בו זוהם הקדירה והקלחת לצדדין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:1.english: Who explained to us [the term] zuhama listeron - It is taught in Seder Tohorot (Kelim 12:2 and 25:3), and I did not know what utensil it is, and he taught me that it is a large spoon with which one pushes the scum of the pot and the cauldron to the sides.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:2.hebrew: קרע מאניה - קרע שאין מתאחה, כדין תלמיד על הרב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:2.english: Rent his garment - A tear that cannot be mended, in accordance with the law of a student [mourning] for [his] teacher.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:3.hebrew: אחד יורד לאמת השחי - משנה היא במסכת תמיד (פרק ג משנה ו) אצל הנכנסים שחרית לפתוח דלתות ההיכל: "מי שזכה בדישון מזבח הפנימי כו', ושני מפתחות בידו, אחד יורד לאמת השחי ואחד פותח כיון". אחד מן המפתחות הללו פותח פשפש הצפוני שאצל פתח ההיכל, בקרן מזרחית צפונית של אולם והיכל, כדתנן התם: "שני פשפשים היה לו לשער הגדול, אחד לצפון ההיכל והאולם ואחד לדרומו, ואותו שבדרום לא נכנס בו אדם מעולם", כדמפרש התם. ואותו פשפש שבצפון — והוא לפתח שבזוית האולם שאצל חמש אמות של כותל ההיכל שבצפון פתח ההיכל, ודלת סובבת בו — ואותו מפתח של אותו הפתח יורד לאמת השחי. פשפשים — פתחים קטנים כמין כיפות קטנות, ארכו כעובי רוחב הכותל, ודלת סובבת בו, פושטי"ר בלעז. אחד יורד לאמת השחי. הבא לפתוח בו שחרית [פשפש שבזוית האולם], עומד מבחוץ בתוך האולם, ומכניס ידו בחור שבכותל עד בית שחיו, ופותח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:3.english: One goes down to the armpit - It is a Mishnah in Tractate Tamid (Chapter 3, Mishnah 6) regarding those who enter in the morning to open the doors of the Sanctuary [Heikhal]: "He who merited the clearing of the ashes of the inner altar, etc., and two keys are in his hand: one goes down to the armpit, and one opens directly." One of these keys opens the northern wicket that is next to the entrance of the Sanctuary, in the northeastern corner of the Antechamber [Ulam] and the Sanctuary, as we learned in a Mishnah there: "The Great Gate had two wickets, one to the north of the Sanctuary and the Antechamber, and one to its south; and the one on the south, no person ever entered through it," as it explains there. And that northern wicket — which is [the one] for the entrance in the corner of the Antechamber, next to the five cubits of the Sanctuary wall to the north of the Sanctuary entrance, and a door pivots in it — that key of that entrance goes down to the armpit. Wickets are small openings, like small arches, whose length is like the thickness of the width of the wall, and a door pivots in it — *postier* in Old French [a postern gate]. One goes down to the armpit: One who comes to open it in the morning [the wicket in the corner of the Antechamber] stands outside within the Antechamber, inserts his hand into the hole in the wall up to his armpit, and opens [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:4.hebrew: ואחד פותח כיון - לאחר שנכנס בזה ובא לו לתא אשר על פני אחת עשרה אמה של אולם קצת מן ההיכל, ופותח במפתח שני דלת אחד שמן התא להיכל מהר בלא טורח כשאר פתחים, ונכנס להיכל לפתוח דלתות ההיכל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:4.english: And one opens directly - After he enters through this [small door] and comes into the chamber that faces the eleven cubits of the Ulam [Entrance Hall], a small part of the Heichal [Sanctuary], he opens with the second key a door that [leads] from the chamber to the Heichal, quickly [and] without difficulty, like other doors, and enters the Heichal to open the doors of the Heichal.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:5.hebrew: כיון - כמו (פסחים לז.) "יעשנה בדפוס ויקבענה כיון", מהר בלא טורח. והאי "שער הגדול" הוא פתח ההיכל שבין אולם להיכל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:13:5.english: Directly [keivan] - Like [the passage in] (Pesachim 37a): "He shall make it in a mold and set it directly [keivan]," [meaning] quickly, without trouble. And this "great gate" is the entrance of the Sanctuary, which is between the Entrance Hall [Ulam] and the Sanctuary [Heichal].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:14:1.hebrew: עומדין זה מפני זה - כדין תלמיד לרב, לפי שהיו יושבין תמיד בבית המדרש יחד ומקשין ומפרקין, וכולם למדים זה מזה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:14:1.english: Rise before one another - As [is] the law of a student toward a teacher, because they would always sit together in the study hall, raising difficulties and resolving [them], and they all learn from one another.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:14:2.hebrew: לרבו מובהק - שרוב חכמתו ממנו, כר"י:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:14:2.english: To his preeminent teacher - [One] from whom most of his wisdom [comes], in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:15:1.english: And his teacher needs him - [In] that [the student] heard from others traditions that are in his possession.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:15:2.english: What [is the law] - That is to say, [does his teacher] take precedence over his father regarding a lost item?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:17:1.hebrew: ותנן רבו שלמדו חכמה - סתמא כר' מאיר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:17:1.english: And we learned: His teacher who taught him wisdom - [This is] an unattributed [mishna] in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:17:2.hebrew: רוב חכמתו - אם מקרא, מקרא; אם משנה, משנה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:17:2.english: The majority of his wisdom - If [it is] Scripture, [then] Scripture; if Mishnah, [then] Mishnah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:18:1.english: A virtue - It is [only] a little [bit of a virtue].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:18:2.hebrew: ואינה מדה - שהמשנה וגמרא יפים ממנה, מפני שתלוין בגירסא ומשתכחים. שבימיהם לא היה גמרא בכתב, וגם לא היה ניתן לכתוב, אלא לפי שנתמעטו הלבבות, התחילו דורות [אחרונים] לכתבו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:18:2.english: And [it is] not a virtue - Because the Mishnah and Gemara are better than it, since they depend on oral memorization and are [easily] forgotten. For in their days, the Gemara was not in writing, nor was it permitted to be written; rather, because hearts diminished [in understanding], [later] generations began to write it down.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:18:3.hebrew: גמרא - כבר פירשתי למעלה שהוא לתת לב להבין סתימות טעמי המשנה מה הם, וכששתים סותרות זו את זו יבין לתרץ שיהיו שתיהן קיימות, או לדעת דברי התנאים החלוקים בדבר, ונימא: הא מני? פלוני חכם הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:18:3.english: Gemara - I have already explained above that it is to pay attention to understand what the unstated reasons of the Mishnah are, and when two [Mishnayot] contradict each other, he will understand how to resolve [them] so that both of them stand, or to know the statements of the Tannaim who disagree on the matter, and we say: "Whose [opinion] is this? It is Sage so-and-so."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:1:1.english: Collapsed - It is a [chance] occurrence for it that it is collapsed under its burden this time.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:1:2.english: But not a habitual collapser - [One] that is accustomed to this.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:1:3.hebrew: ולא מפורק - והוא צריך טעינה, ולקמן פריך: הכתיב "הקם תקים":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:1:3.english: And not [when it is] unloaded - and it needs loading, and later [the Gemara] asks: Is it not written, "You shall surely raise [it] up"?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:5:1.english: I might [have thought] from a distance - And [the verse] imposed upon him [the obligation] to go there.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33a:6:1.english: Walks slowly with him - After he has loaded it, lest [the burden] fall again.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:14:1.hebrew: ומקרעין זה על זה - אף על פי שאינו יודע יותר, לפי שלומדין זה מזה. ואם תאמר, דאמרינן בפרק האורג (שבת דף קה: ושם): חייב לקרוע על אדם כשר אפילו לא היה בשעת יציאת נשמה? ויש לומר, דהכא מיירי בקרע שאינו מתאחה, כדין תלמיד על רבו; וכן פירש רש"י:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:14:1.english: And they rend [their garments] over one another - Even though one does not know more [than the other], because they learn from one another. And if you ask that we say in the chapter [entitled] HaOreg (Shabbat 105b and there [in the parallel passages]): one is obligated to rend [his garment] for a worthy person even if he was not [present] at the time of the departure of the soul? One can say that here it is dealing with a rend that may not be mended, like the law of a student [rending] for his teacher, and so Rashi explained.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:1:1.hebrew: מה לי רבצן - וא"ת: ולישני "רובץ" בחנם, "רבצן" בשכר, דה"נ משני "ולא מפורק" בחנם אלא בשכר? וי"ל, דניחא ליה לשנויי דאתי כרבי יוסי הגלילי, כדמוכח דאתיא כוותיה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:1:1.english: "What is it to me [if it is] a habitual collapser" - And if you ask: Let [the Gemara] answer [that one must assist] a "collapsed" [animal] for free, [and] a "habitual collapser" for remuneration, for so too it answers [below regarding] "but not [when it is] unloaded" — [not] for free, rather for remuneration? And one can say that it is preferable for [the Gemara] to answer that [the baraita] accords with Rabbi Yosei HaGalili, as it [subsequently] proves that [the baraita] accords with him.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:5:1.hebrew: וזהו ריס - אית דגרסי רוס, דשבע ומחצה רוס עולה אלפים, דהוי שיעור מיל, כדמוכח בפרק שני שעירי (יומא דף סז.) גבי סוכות דשעיר המשתלח:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:5:1.english: And that is a ris - There are those who read [the text as] ros, for seven and a half ros amounts to two thousand [cubits], which is the measure of a mil, as is evident in the chapter [entitled] Shnei Se'irei (Yoma 67a) regarding the booths of the scapegoat.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:6:1.hebrew: ונוטל שכר - במה שמדדה, ובפריקה מיירי שירא פן ירבץ; דאי בטעינה — פשיטא, דהא טעינה גופה בשכר, וכל שכן מה שמדדה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:6:1.english: And he takes remuneration - For walking with [the animal]; and [the baraita] is dealing with unloading, where he fears lest it crouch [under its burden]. For if [it were speaking] of loading, [this would be] obvious, since loading itself is for remuneration, and all the more so walking with [it].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:7:1.hebrew: אבדתו קודמת - וא"ת: אבדתו ואבדת רבו וכבוד אביו, איזהו קודם? אי אבדתו — הלא כבוד אביו עדיף, למאן דאמר בפ"ק דקדושין (דף לב. ושם) משל בן! ואם כבוד אביו — הלא אבדת רבו קודמת, כדאמר לעיל: "אני ה'"! ויש לומר: אבדתו קודמת; דהיכא דאביו נהנה מגוף הבהמה חייב לכבדו, כגון: "שחוט לי בהמתך", אבל "הניחה ליאבד ותביא לי לאכול" — אינו חייב, שגם לאב קשה האבדה, אלא שרוצה לאכול:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33a:7:1.english: "His lost item takes precedence" - And if you ask: [If one is faced with] his own lost item, his teacher's lost item, and honoring his father, which one takes precedence? If [you say] his own lost item — is not honoring his father superior, according to the one who says in the first chapter of Kiddushin (32a and there) [that honoring parents is] at the son's expense? And if [you say] honoring his father — does not his teacher's lost item take precedence, as [the Gemara] stated above: "I am the Lord"? And one can say: His own lost item takes precedence; for where his father benefits from the animal itself, he is obligated to honor him, such as [if the father says,] "Slaughter your animal for me"; however, [if he says,] "Leave it to be lost and bring me [food] to eat" — [he is not obligated to do so], for the loss is also distressing to the father, [and he does not benefit from the loss itself,] rather he simply wants to eat.
